subject.title: feat: Let users steer running ACP/sub-agent sessions from Discord (and other chat surfaces)

question: Should the remaining fix be a coordinated refresh of the admission-layer path in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89238, a narrower split for ACP/subagent thread-bound Discord sessions, or closure of this issue under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48003?
rationale: The remaining behavior crosses channel serialization, active-run queue policy, fallback delivery, and session-state recovery, so an automated fix should not choose the permanent ownership boundary or accepted fallback semantics alone.

options.title: Refresh the admission-layer fix
options.body: Rebase or replace https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89238, preserve the merged active/non-streaming fixes, and explicitly encode accepted queued/steered turns so fallback delivery does not double-send.

options.title: Split ACP/thread-bound scope
options.body: Keep this issue as the ACP/subagent Discord-thread tracker and let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48003 own only generic ordinary-message queue steering.

options.title: Close under the canonical steer issue
options.body: Treat this issue as fully covered by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48003 and move any remaining ACP-specific evidence there before closing.

recommendation.title: Refresh the admission-layer fix
recommendation.body: Rebase or replace https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89238, preserve the merged active/non-streaming fixes, and explicitly encode accepted queued/steered turns so fallback delivery does not double-send.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is tied to the related steering replacement and recent session-state recovery path that the remaining fix must preserve.
